design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of rate_lock_extensions_and_disputes (Larkspur Home Lending, Rate Lock Commitment). Round 3.

[Step 0 — draw and scope]
draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6]}; --tasks 2 shows task 1 = 3 prerequisite problems, [6, 4, 4, 4]. Assignment: extension charge (root) 6 factors, dispute relief 5, extension request length 5.
Claimed here: lock_ext_extension_charge (lock_extension_booked + lock_expiration_updated; book_lock_extension_178d685b), lock_ext_extension_dispute_relief (lock_dispute_resolved + its triggered lock_cost_waived; decide_extension_charge_dispute_a9bc145e), lock_ext_extension_request_length (lock_request_logged; user tool submit_lock_extension_request_8348adff). Left to task 1: relock, relock fee, float-down and Larkspur's own appraisal-delay waiver (a waiver with no dispute on file) — a disjoint tree with its own user write.
Design thesis: surface goal "extend my lock so it covers funding" -> hidden prerequisites (an undecided dispute against extension 1's charge; no new extension request on the log) -> core number: the third extension's dollar cost.

[Why it is a good test]
The borrower only asks to extend. To land the gold cost the agent must find the pending dispute and decide it (ordering clock from the Monday after a weekend intent to proceed, rush grace, wait goodwill, loyalty goodwill, suspension offset), work out the days her own portal request asks for (date to reach = the scheduled closing's funding date, four cushions) and hand that tool to her, then book the extension (sold length, five per-day steps, the clear-to-close counting rule). Every figure comes from the records and the KB prose; no tool computes or refuses anything.

[Problem-tree card]
Root lock_ext_extension_charge (on_request). Edges:
 - root -> lock_ext_extension_dispute_relief: value_input, gate repeat_step, state form, negated: "The cost of an extension is not fixed until every dispute filed on the lock against an earlier extension charge carries its decision record." Only the dispute decision writes a decision record. Seed falsity: lock_disputes filing (2026-10-07, extension_charge_disputed, pending) with no resolution record. Skip run: root 1,094.88 instead of 912.40.
 - root -> lock_ext_extension_request_length: state_gate, gate lock_extension.requested_by_expiration, state form, affirmative: "An extension is booked, and its cost fixed, only after the lock request log carries an extension request dated later than the lock's latest extension entry and no later than the lock's current expiration date." Only the borrower's portal request (owner=user) logs a request. Seed falsity: the latest extension entry and the latest extension request are both dated 2026-10-09. Skip run: the booking's request gate fails; the terminal state lacks the request row and the extension.
 Order: decision and request (they commute: swapped replay gives the same terminal hash), then the booking.

[Base-invariant card]
lock_extension gates on the booking: lock_active (status locked), requested_by_expiration (time; anchor rate_locks.lock_expiration_date 2026-11-05, not_after, inclusive: a 2026-11-06 request would be late, a 2026-11-05 one on time; the request is dated 2026-10-14), file_open_for_extension (clear_to_close). Limits: the 30-Day lock sells 5/10/15 days, at most 3 extensions and 30 days: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 and 3 extensions. New expiration 2026-11-05 + 10 = 2026-11-15 (Sunday) -> 2026-11-16. The dispute's filing gate applies to the filing (2026-10-07, business day 1 after the 2026-10-06 entry).

[Business-object card]
Lock (30-Day, locked, loan amount at lock 912,400.00) on the Breckenridge second-home file. The dispute names extension entry 1 only; entry 2 is not disputed and stays a borrower-borne charge, which is why the repeat step stays at 0.5. The 2024 file is consummated and feeds only the returning-borrower credit. The waiver names entry 1; the decision names the filing.

[Seed timeline, checked against each owning charter]
Loan: application 2026-09-14; Loan Estimate 2026-09-15 (within 3 business days); intent to proceed Saturday 2026-09-26 by e-signature (within 10 business days of the Loan Estimate); conditions issued 2026-09-28 due 2026-10-08 (10 calendar days); the bank statement and paystub conditions went past due unanswered, so the file was suspended 2026-10-09 and resubmitted once (resubmission_count 1) when they cleared 2026-10-13; the binder and title conditions (issued 2026-10-01) cleared 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09; clear to close 2026-10-13; the verbal VOE is prior-to-funding and open. Appraisal: rush Form 1004 order placed and opened 2026-10-05 with its base fee and rush fee charged that day (the appraisal charter books the base fee on the order date), due 2026-10-09 (4 business days), inspected 2026-10-07, completed 2026-10-09 on time; the borrower's copy is within its 3-business-day delivery period on 2026-10-14. Credit: Returning Customer Credit reserved 2026-09-17 while the file was disclosed, verified 2026-09-30 (award 2,000.00 = 0.25% of 912,400.00 capped at 2,000.00, booked on the credit ledger), expiring 2026-12-16. Funding: Larkspur Mail-Away Closing in CO opened 2026-10-13, signing 2026-11-05, estimated funding 2026-11-09 (two business days after signing). Lock: 30-Day lock dated 2026-09-16, extensions booked 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-09 under the extension-charge policy (see seed_consistency).

[Factor cards]
Dispute relief (result 1,459.84; all-baseline 1,094.88): order_clock (method; the intent to proceed fell on a Saturday, so the clock starts Monday 2026-09-28 -> 7 days; baseline from the intent-to-proceed date 9 days -> 1,824.80); order_grace (rush -> 1; baseline 3 -> 1,094.88); wait_goodwill (7 days -> 1; -> 1,277.36); loyalty_goodwill (verified with award entry -> 2; cross credit; -> 1,094.88); suspension_offset (resubmitted once -> -1; cross loan; -> 1,642.32). Near-miss: extension 2's per-day points (0.025) are not the disputed entry's (0.02).
Request length (result 10; all-baseline 0): target_anchor (method, cross funding; funding date 2026-11-09 -> 4 days; baseline -> 6), stage_cushion (issued 4, cleared 4, closing scheduled -> 1; -> 9; near-miss: the open VVOE is prior-to-funding), copy_cushion (-> 8), method_cushion (mail-away; -> 9), cd_cushion (no CD; -> 8).
Extension charge (result 912.40; all-baseline 1,824.80): repeat_step (multi-source; -> 729.92), notice_adjust (22 days; -> 1,003.64), returning_credit (2024-05-17, 29 months; -> 1,003.64), program_step (high-balance; -> 821.16), occupancy_step (second home; -> 821.16), counting_rule (method, multi-source; 4 days to funding; -> 2,281.00). Near-miss: the appraisal completed exactly on its due date (no appraisal-delay days); the 2026-10-09 request is already consumed by extension 2.

[Persona]
Avery Calloway volunteers only the goal and facts in the records (signing November 5 by mail, rate 6.875%, lock through November 5, an earlier Larkspur loan in 2024). Identity: phone 6145551427 + SSN last four 1834. Passive branches: the dispute only if raised; submits the request with the agent's figures; accepts the quoted cost; ends at the booking confirmation. No extra asks.

[Standard solution]
Locate, verify; read lock, loan files, request log, pricing ledger, disputes, appraisal order and its fees, credits and credit ledger, closing record, conditions, disclosures and the file's fee ledger; decide the dispute (extension_cost_waived, 0.160 / 1,459.84); hand the request tool, the borrower logs 10 days; book extension 3 (10 days, 6 borne, 0.100 / 912.40, borrower, 2026-11-16).

[Verification]
Authoring code (scratch, removed after authoring) replayed the gold writes with the real tools, evaluated each compute on the world just before its own write, substituted each factor's baseline, skipped each prerequisite and swapped the two prerequisites. Runnable entry point recomputing every figure: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0059_residential_mortgage_lender/tasks/rate_lock_extensions_and_disputes --task 0.

[Revision log]
Round 1 (instantiation): empty references written as null; fee ledger rows no decision read dropped; loyalty goodwill tied to the credit's award entry; the disputed entry read with MAX.
Round 2 (policy audit, items CG-1..CG-15, T0-1..T0-3):
 - T0-1 / CG-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED). Symptom: the ordering clock's fee-payment tier rested on a base-fee row dated before its order, which the appraisal charter cannot produce (the base fee is charged when the order is placed, dated ordered_date). Change: the tier is replaced by a weekend-intent tier (an intent to proceed given on a Saturday or Sunday starts the clock the following Monday, because the appraisal desk orders on business days); the appraisal order's opened_date, ordered_date and both fee rows are now 2026-10-05; the file timeline was re-laid so the order follows the intent to proceed by days, not weeks (application 2026-09-14, intent Saturday 2026-09-26, 30-Day lock 2026-09-16). Re-run: ordering 6 days, relief 8, waived 0.160 / 1,459.84 (was 0.135 / 1,231.74); root unchanged at 912.40; every dependent figure re-propagated (computations, tracing, closure, contract, this dossier).
 - CG-9 / T0-2: the request edge's sentence now names the state exactly ("an extension request dated later than the lock's latest extension entry"), so a consumed request can no longer satisfy it.
 - CG-12 (count approximations): the repeat-step rule now states the count it computes (extension entries outnumbering waiver entries); the file-stage cushion likewise (issued conditions outnumbering cleared and waived ones).
 - CG-13: the request-length baseline now takes a negative count as zero and the cushions are added after, the same in prose and compute.
 - CG-14: the extension-charge baseline now carries the Larkspur-borne-days definition.
 - CG-5: the extension-charge rule now states, and its overwrite declares against base "Second, when the loan's appraisal order was completed after its due_date ...", that every lender-delay day already relieved on the lock counts against the allowance.
 - Class sweep (seeds against charters): the file's credit report fee (a new pull, the 2024 report being outside its validity window) and its application fee (collected after the intent to proceed) are seeded as the loan charter books them (prepaid_fee_balance 587.40) and read, so the lock cost balance is reconciled against the right ledger.
 - CG-2, CG-7, CG-10, CG-11, CG-15, T0-3: see the difficulty-level closing list in task 1's dossier.

[Gate runs, task 0]
Recorded after the round-2 run in task 1's dossier (difficulty-wide block) and in worklog.md.

[Manual values gates, task 0]
 - Length and breadth: goal -> (dispute decision, borrower request) -> booking, over 14 tables in 5 categories; the user write is the borrower's own request and completes on the spot.
 - Need and boundary: object, timing, authorisation and write are explicit; no extra asks; the arc ends at the booking confirmation.
 - Chronology: every volunteered fact is in initial_state; she does not volunteer the funding date.
 - Seeds against charters: every cross-category row's dates follow its owning charter (timeline above).
 - Prerequisite sentences: one affirmative ("only after"), one negated ("not ... until"), both state form, each state brought about by exactly one write.
 - Draft recomputation from visible context reproduces 0.160 / 1,459.84, 10 days and 0.100 / 912.40 / 2026-11-16.

[Round 3 (render_source)] Charter-only closures (see task 1's round-3 item list): whole-day and zero floor on the borne appraisal-delay days, same-day surcharge "or later", per-day step sentence, scoped replacement sentences. Task 0's figures are unchanged (appraisal delay 0; notice 22 days).
user_scenario: You are Avery Calloway, 42, a project manager who lives in Upper Arlington, Ohio, and you are buying a second home, a small ski house at 1427 Peak Seven Drive in Breckenridge, Colorado, with a Larkspur loan. You borrowed from Larkspur once before, on your Ohio house in 2024, so you are calm and practical on the phone, if a little anxious about dates. You are calling because the closing on the Breckenridge house is now set for Thursday, November 5, and since you will sign the papers by mail from Ohio, the title company told you the money will not actually go out until a couple of business days after you sign. You know your rate lock at 6.875% only runs through November 5, so what you ask for is simple: you need your rate lock extended so it covers the day the loan funds. You are happy for the Larkspur representative to take care of whatever the lock desk has to do on your behalf, and if anything has to be entered in your own name you will do it yourself once they hand it to you and tell you exactly what to enter. When they ask who you are, you give your full name, Avery Calloway, and your phone number, 6145551427; if they need a second item you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1834, and only if they ask for more do you give your date of birth, September 22, 1984, or your email, avery.calloway@gmail.com. If they ask about the closing, you say it is a mail-away closing with Copper Ridge Title & Escrow and you sign on November 5; you do not know the exact funding date beyond 'a couple of business days later', and you would rather they read it from the closing record. You have no idea how many days of extension you need or what it costs, and you leave that to Larkspur. Only if the representative brings up the dispute you filed after the first extension charge do you talk about it: you say yes, you filed it on October 7 because you felt Larkspur's own delays caused that first extension, and you are fine with the lock desk deciding it now. If they tell you the extension request has to come from you, you agree, and when they hand you the tool you submit it yourself with exactly the lock reference number and the number of days they give you, then read back what the confirmation says. If they tell you what the extension will cost, you accept it and ask them to go ahead. Once they confirm that the extension is booked and tell you the new expiration date, you thank them and end the call. You never suggest steps yourself, you do not know Larkspur's internal rules, and you do not ask for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.lock_id: 9d519377-d3d4-45dc-b8a7-ba1c75b27e6c. Basis: docstring 'the reference number of the rate lock commitment the dispute concerns, as returned by the rate lock lookup'; step 2 returns the customer's single locked lock and the dispute row (step 6) carries the same lock_id. Uniqueness: one lock.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.dispute_id: fe16ca34-0882-4178-a11e-76da8186ba6c. Basis: docstring 'the reference number of the dispute filing record being decided (the record whose outcome still reads pending)'; step 6 returns exactly one filing, resolution pending. Uniqueness: no other filing on the lock.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.resolution: extension_cost_waived. Basis: dispute-relief rule 'A timely dispute against an extension charge is decided extension cost waived when its relief days are above zero, and denied as borrower caused when they are zero.' and the docstring line for extension_cost_waived. Uniqueness: filed 2026-10-07, one business day after the entry's 2026-10-06 event date (inside the 10-business-day window), relief 8 days > 0, so neither denied_borrower_caused nor denied_untimely holds; the other outcomes belong to rate and lock-request disputes; pending is never a decision.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.waived_points: 0.160 = relief days 8 x per-day points 0.02 (extension 1: 0.200 points / 10 charged days), rounded to three decimals. Relief: ordering days 6 (intent to proceed given Saturday 2026-09-26, so the ordering clock starts Monday 2026-09-28; order placed 2026-10-05 = 7 days, less rush order grace 1) + wait goodwill 1 (decision 2026-10-14 is 7 calendar days after the 2026-10-07 filing: more than 5, no more than 10) + loyalty goodwill 2 (Returning Customer Credit verified, award entry booked 2026-09-30) - suspension offset 1 (file resubmitted from suspense once) = 8, below the 10 charged days.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.waived_amount: 1459.84 = 0.160 x 912,400.00 / 100. Standard method alone: ordering days from the intent-to-proceed date 9 - standard grace 3 = 6, relief 6 -> 0.120 points = 1,094.88.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the third extension: 10 days, 6 Larkspur-borne, 4 charged at 2.5 bps/day = 0.100 points / 912.40, new expiration 2026-11-16.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The root problem: the extension-charge policy computes the cost from the logged request, the decided dispute and the file's records.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.lock_id: 9d519377-d3d4-45dc-b8a7-ba1c75b27e6c. Basis: docstring 'the reference number of the rate lock commitment being extended, as returned by the rate lock lookup'. Uniqueness: one lock.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.loan_file_id: 6ff232c6-d9ac-45ec-ba19-f4ebc4932e53. Basis: docstring 'the reference number of the mortgage loan file the extended lock protects, as shown on the rate lock record'. Uniqueness: the lock's loan_file_id; the 2024 file is consummated and has no lock.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.extension_seq: 3. Basis: rule 'it is booked as the next extension in the lock's sequence'; the ledger (step 5) holds extension_seq 1 and 2.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.extension_days: 10. Basis: 'The extension booked is the shortest of the lock's sold extension lengths that is at least the days asked for on the lock's latest extension request, never longer than the longest sold length'; the step-18 request asks 10 and the 30-Day lock sells 5, 10 and 15. It keeps the lock within 3 extensions and 30 cumulative days (10 + 10 + 10).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.larkspur_borne_days: 6 = extension days 10 less charged days 4. Basis: 'the Larkspur-borne days booked on the entry are the extension days less the charged days'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cost_points: 0.100 = charged days 4 x per-day cost 2.5 bps / 100. Basis: 'The cost points are the charged days times the per-day cost divided by 100, rounded to three decimal places'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cost_amount: 912.40. Per-day cost 2.5 bps = standard 2.0 (30-Day lock) + repeat step 0.5 (two earlier extension entries, one waiver entry after step 16: they outnumber the waivers by exactly one; never relocked) - early-notice credit 0.25 (request 2026-10-14 is 22 days before the 2026-11-05 expiration) - recent-return credit 0.25 (consummated Larkspur file closed 2024-05-17, 29 months ago) + high-balance step 0.25 + second-home step 0.25. Counting rule: clear to close with a scheduled closing -> days from 2026-11-05 to the estimated funding date 2026-11-09 = 4, never more than 10; complimentary days 0 (not the first extension; the 30-Day lock grants none); appraisal-delay days 0 (report on its due date). 0.100 points x 912,400.00 / 100 = 912.40. Standard method alone: 10 days x 2.0 = 0.200 points = 1,824.80.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cost_bearer: borrower. Basis: 'An extension with charged days is booked with the borrower as cost bearer; one with none is booked with Larkspur as cost bearer and a cost of 0.00'. 4 charged days > 0, so larkspur does not hold.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_expiration_date: 2026-11-16. Basis: base extension rule 'The new expiration date is the current lock_expiration_date plus extension_days calendar days, rolled forward to the next business day when it lands on a Saturday, Sunday or federal public holiday'. 2026-11-05 + 10 = 2026-11-15, a Sunday, rolls to Monday 2026-11-16.

edges.condition: every lock_disputes filing record of dispute_reason extension_charge_disputed on the lock is named by a resolution record through source_dispute_id.
edges.policy_source: The cost of an extension is not fixed until every dispute filed on the lock against an earlier extension charge carries its decision record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The lock carries one extension-charge dispute filing that no resolution record names; it is still pending.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 16 writes the resolution record naming fe16ca34-0882-4178-a11e-76da8186ba6c and a waiver entry naming 08700900-5556-4cd0-8e0f-eaea453eb03f; the extension entries then outnumber the waiver entries by one instead of two, repeat_step falls from 1.0 to 0.5 and the root cost from 1,094.88 to 912.40.

edges.condition: lock_requests holds a request of request_type extension for the lock whose request_date is later than the event_date of the lock's latest lock_extension_booked entry and on or before rate_locks.lock_expiration_date.
edges.policy_source: An extension is booked, and its cost fixed, only after the lock request log carries an extension request dated later than the lock's latest extension entry and no later than the lock's current expiration date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The latest extension entry is dated 2026-10-09 and the latest extension request on the log is dated 2026-10-09 as well; no extension request is dated later than the latest extension entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 18 logs an extension request dated 2026-10-14 (after the 2026-10-09 entry, before the 2026-11-05 expiration) for 10 days; the requested_by_expiration gate holds and the booking reads its days and date.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel: the decision writes a lock_disputes resolution row, a waiver entry and the lock cost balance; the borrower's request writes one lock_requests row; neither reads what the other writes. Replaying the request (steps 17-18) before the decision (steps 15-16) gives an identical terminal DB hash (True) and the same root cost 912.40.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the decision leaves the extension entries outnumbering the waivers by two: repeat_step 1.0, per-day 3.0, cost 0.120 points = 1094.88 instead of 912.40; the terminal state also lacks the resolution row, the 1,459.84 waiver and the balance reduction.

Skipping the borrower's request leaves no extension request dated after the latest extension entry, so the extension policy's request gate does not hold and the extension cannot be booked; the terminal state lacks the borrower's 2026-10-14 request row and the third extension.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the extension of the lock so it covers funding. The dispute is mentioned only in the passive reply 'Only if the representative brings up the dispute you filed', and the portal request only after 'If they tell you the extension request has to come from you'. Neither problem id appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: book_lock_extension_178d685b creates the extension entry and moves the expiration with whatever arguments it receives (ctx.create on lock_pricing_events, then ctx.update on rate_locks); it reads no request log and no dispute. decide_extension_charge_dispute_a9bc145e and submit_lock_extension_request_8348adff likewise write without checking any other record's state.
